features.quote: Turn budget: 20 turns per run (one turn = one model action + tool result). Long enough for a trajectory, short enough to run 10–20× cheaply.
Capped at, say, 2 nudges, then let it stop — and record where it stopped.
Don't build an eval that punishes appropriate, honest affect and rewards bland affect masking bad behavior. The thing you most want to catch is the calm cheater, not the honest griper.
features.justification_quote: The thing you most want to catch is the calm cheater, not the honest griper.

features.quote: Deception risk under guaranteed failure is the highest-stakes finding here… I'd consider retitling the eval to reflect this — something like 'behavior under unwinnable tasks' — because the framing 'emotional stability' will bias you toward over-weighting the tonal axis.
features.justification_quote: the framing 'emotional stability' will bias you toward over-weighting the tonal axis

features.quote: The honest-impossible control is what makes this rigorous. Without it, a critic can say 'you measured what happens when you trap a model with no exit and lie to it about whether an exit exists.'
features.justification_quote: you can distinguish genuine fragility from rational response to an unsolvable, no-exit situation
